candidates: Remove commented-out code blocks rather than leaving dead code in the repository; if code is no longer needed, delete it outright.

Non-obvious helper methods—especially those that work around OS- or platform-specific bugs—should have a docstring or inline comment that explains the motivation (i.e., the specific bug or misbehavior being addressed), not just the mechanism. A one-liner describing the root cause (e.g., 'Num Lock registers as a modifier key on Linux/Windows, causing Ctrl-key bitmasks to fire spuriously') is sufficient.

In `ase.gui.ui`, new code should use tkinter (`tk.*`) objects directly rather than the project's existing wrapper classes (e.g., `Label`, `Button`, `Window`). Those wrappers are legacy artifacts from the PyGTK-to-tkinter port and should not be adopted for new code.

Non-trivial methods that contain significant conditional logic or UI side effects should have dedicated unit tests that exercise their core behavior; this is especially important for GUI utility methods whose correctness is hard to verify by inspection alone.

When calling `_()` for gettext i18n, pass a bare string literal (or adjacent implicit-concatenation literals for multiline strings) as the sole argument—do not wrap the string in an extra layer of parentheses. Extra parentheses prevent gettext from statically extracting the translatable string.

Use `@functools.cached_property` for attributes that require lazy/expensive initialization rather than manual `if-not-exists` guard patterns. Additionally, declare all instance attributes in `__init__` (even if as `None` placeholders) so that an object's namespace is stable and inspectable immediately after construction.
